references.text: Abimelech, the son of Gideon's concubine, later becomes a central figure who kills his brothers and becomes king in Shechem.
The preceding verse mentions Gideon's seventy sons from his many wives, providing context for the concubine in Shechem.
Concubines (pilegesh) are also mentioned in connection with Nahor, showing this practice during the patriarchal period.
Abraham also had concubines, and their sons received gifts but not the primary inheritance, similar to Abimelech's situation.
Bilhah is mentioned as Jacob's concubine, showing that concubines had an acknowledged but subordinate status.
Jotham refers to Abimelech as 'son of his slave woman,' showing his lower status compared to the other sons.
